Jones, D.S.J. and Pujadó, P.R. (eds) (2006). Handbook of Petroleum Processing. Springer, Dordrecht. 1357 pp. ISBN 978-1-4020-2819-9 (hardback), 978-1-4020-2820-5 (e-book). Copy held is the 2008 reprint; no DOI printed on the copyright page.

Targeted pass (text layer good). Locators are PRINTED page numbers (PDF page = printed + 7 to 14, varying with unnumbered figure pages). The book is a design-method handbook: it has NO licensor utilities/investment tables like Meyers 1997 or Gary 2007, and NO sulfur recovery chapter (the SRU appears only as a process description, pp.36-37, and as a unit in the example refinery, Table 2.31; Claus tail gas, utilities and cost are absent). Loaded: Table 17.1.5 approximate utilities per bbl feed (steam, power, fuel) for reformer, naphtha and diesel HDS, thermal cracker, FCC, VDU, light ends, splitter, wash plants (screening factors, author's own); Table 2.31 service factors (loaded as capacity-factor) for CDU, VDU, HDS, reformer, thermal cracker, FCC, isom/alky, gas treating and sulfur recovery (95%) plus SRU design capacity; UOP SR vs CCR Platforming WAIT temperatures, on-stream hours and hydrogen yield; FCC regenerator temperatures (partial/full burn) and max-olefins FCC temperature; hydrocracking and hydrotreating SOR temperature ranges; HF alkylation isostripper reboiler process temperature; Par-Isom revamp incremental capex (4Q1997 USGC); MEA stripper temperature; thermal cracker/visbreaker/delayed coker coil outlet temperatures; residue hydrocracker test-run temperatures and makeup hydrogen; fired heater efficiency classes (LHV); standard motor efficiencies (Table 18.21). Not loaded (in _other-values): the capital cost factors of Ch. 17.1.2, which the source itself calls "pure fiction"; the thermal cracker estimate built on them; utility costs per day (no price year); water and labour; SR/CCR economics; FCC regenerator inventories; amine steam per gallon of solution; thermal cracker heater sizing example (internal inconsistency: summary table lists section 2 duty 48.633 = steam enthalpy instead of 16.652). Heating-value basis is not stated for refinery fuel; fired heater efficiencies are LHV (process heaters usually LHV, p.1048). Dashes in Table 17.1.5 are not loaded as zero. Chapters 5-9 were written by UOP authors; Figure 5.7 is reprinted with permission from UOP; the Par-Isom case appears to come from Gosling et al. 1997 (chapter reference 4) but the source does not say so. No numbers are explicitly reprinted from Gary & Handwerk.
